newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Santer says Renault did not follow spirit of law.
newsitem.headline: Santer says Renault did not follow spirit of law.

text.p: European Commission President Jaques Santer said on Wednesday that French car maker Renault had not followed the spirit of EU laws in the way it went about closing a plant in Belgium.
"Mr Santer regrets the way in which Renault have managed the closure," said his spokesman, Nikolaus van der Pas. "The spirit of the law was not respected."
The statement could be seen as support for the company to be taken to court, Van der Pas said.
"You can take that as encouragement," he said when asked by reporters if the Commission thought Renault had a case to answer.
Van der Pas said, however, that the Commission was not saying specifically whether it believed Renault had broken EU laws related to how management consults workers in the event of a factory closure.
Because two EU directives on worker rights had become national law, it was up to national courts to decide, he said.
It was up to member states or the workers themselves to press the issue, he said.
